notes.text: Kirill Marchenko is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Easton Cowan has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews. That line has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 81:47 together, down from 72% with Marchenko.

Nick Blankenburg is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 12 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Troy Stecher has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson. That pair has had 52% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 71:15 together, about what it had with Blankenburg (48%).
Ryan Tverberg was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside John Tavares and William Nylander.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 24 games, up from 6% last season.
Logan Stanley is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Adam Pelech has taken his spot beside Matthew Schaefer.
Ryan Pulock is out (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, down from 37% last season.

stakes: The Maple Leafs go in tied for seventh in the Atlantic with 19 points, the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan with 25 points.

story.head: Barzal’s favorite opponent
paras: The Maple Leafs are winless in eight (0-7-1), and the Islanders (10-6-5) lost 4-3 in overtime to Winnipeg on Thursday. The teams have split two meetings this season. Going in, the Maple Leafs are last in the Atlantic (tied for 26th in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th).

The Maple Leafs have played better than their record (.396) says: their chances are worth about .483, mostly because they’re 3-9 in one-goal games. The Islanders’ record (.595) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Maple Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). The Islanders, by contrast, have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). They also get their defensemen shooting (1st). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Isles roll four lines, but the Maple Leafs lean on their top six. The Maple Leafs’ power play (10th) could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (29th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Auston Matthews (13 G / 19 A / 32 P in 24 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with five goals in six games against the Islanders since 2023-24. William Nylander (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 21 GP) is next in line.
Anthony Stolarz (5-4-1 / .904 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Toronto. Ilya Sorokin (8-4-2 / .918 SV% in 14 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and will likely start.
